name: Merger and Restructuring Analysis
title: Merger and Restructuring Analysis
answer: Merger and restructuring analysis covers the work of assessing whether a proposed combination, divestiture or reorganisation makes sense and can be completed. It spans target screening, valuation, synergy and cost estimates, financing and capital structure, regulatory clearance, and the integration or separation plan that follows. In this atlas the topic sits inside corporate governance and regulatory compliance, because a deal is judged as much by whether it can be approved and executed as by the price paid.

sections.body: Merger and restructuring analysis covers the work of assessing whether a proposed combination, divestiture or reorganisation makes sense and can be completed. It spans target screening, valuation, synergy and cost estimates, financing and capital structure, regulatory clearance, and the integration or separation plan that follows. In this atlas the topic sits inside corporate governance and regulatory compliance, because a deal is judged as much by whether it can be approved and executed as by the price paid.
sections.heading: Scope

sections.body: The work runs on deal data rooms, financial models in spreadsheets, market and company databases, and the document management systems that hold contracts, filings and correspondence. Larger teams add data extraction and review platforms to read long agreements and regulatory submissions at speed. Outputs are typically board papers, valuation models, diligence reports and clearance filings, all of which have to be traceable back to source documents.
sections.heading: What it runs on

sections.body: Analysts build a view of standalone value, then model the combined entity under different assumptions about revenue, costs and financing. Diligence teams check what is being bought, including contracts, liabilities, intellectual property and pending disputes. Regulatory work maps the deal against competition, foreign investment and sector rules, and integration planning starts before signing so that day one and the first hundred days are sequenced. Machine learning increasingly assists with document review, clause extraction and anomaly detection, but the judgement on price and structure stays with the deal team.
sections.heading: How the work is done

sections.body: Deal governance turns on disclosure, conflicts, fiduciary duties and the allocation of risk between buyer and seller. Boards need a defensible record of how they reached a decision, and advisers need to manage inside information and any related party interests. Regulatory clearance can be conditional, and remedies such as divestitures or behavioural commitments become part of the obligations the combined business must meet. Provenance matters throughout: every figure in a fairness opinion, synergy estimate or clearance submission should be traceable to a document, a model version or a filing.
sections.heading: Rights, risk and provenance

sections.body: Expect more use of automated document review and data room analytics to shorten diligence, and more scrutiny of how AI tools are used to produce or check deal materials. Competition and foreign investment regimes continue to widen their reach, so clearance planning starts earlier and shapes structure. Restructurings are also becoming more common as companies separate businesses or unwind past acquisitions, which puts the same analytical toolkit to work in reverse. The site tracks 153 active AI lawsuits and 29 AI case law precedents, a reminder that disputes over data, models and contracts can sit inside a transaction and change its value.
